name: git-graph
description: A GRAPH tab for the active repository: every branch's commits as a lane graph with their branch, remote and tag labels. Filter by branch, remote, tag or author, find a commit by message, author, hash or ref, click a commit for its changed files and their diffs, and right-click a commit or a ref label to check out, branch, tag, cherry-pick, revert, reset or delete.

gitGraph.pollInterval.description: How often (ms) the open GRAPH tab checks whether any ref moved, reloading only when one did. Runs only while the tab is the active one - an inactive or closed tab makes no requests.

gitGraph.showRemoteBranches.description: Include remote-tracking branches in a graph the first time it is opened. Off draws only local branches, tags and stashes, which on a repository with many stale remote branches is a much shorter graph. The Branches menu in the tab bar changes this per repository, and its choice is remembered from then on.

gitGraph.showTags.description: Include commits that are only reachable from a tag. Same as the Branches menu's Show tags, which overrides this per repository.

gitGraph.showStashes.description: Include stash entries in the graph. Same as the Branches menu's Show stashes, which overrides this per repository.

gitGraph.firstParent.description: Follow only each merge's first parent, so the graph shows the mainline and not the commits that were merged into it. The lanes stay correct - git rewrites the history it walks, it does not drop commits from the middle of one.

gitGraph.commitsPerPage.description: How many commits the graph loads at a time, for the first page and for every Load More after it. Larger pages mean fewer round trips and a longer wait for each one.

gitGraph.dateStyle.description: How the date column reads. The other form is always in the row's tooltip.

gitGraph.showHashColumn.description: Show each commit's short hash as the last column, where VS Code's Git Graph puts it. It stays visible whenever the lanes are hidden - under an author filter, or the find bar's Filter - so a row still has something to read and copy.

gitGraph.showUncommittedChanges.description: Show an Uncommitted Changes row above HEAD whenever the working tree has staged, unstaged or untracked changes. Expand it to see the files; clicking one opens HEAD against the file on disk, which you can edit there.

gitGraph.fileView.description: How an expanded commit lists its changed files: one path per row, or grouped into folders. The button at the right of the graph's toolbar switches this too.
